correctness.rationale: For Q4 with vertices 0..15 adjacent iff XOR has popcount one, independent sets and nonempty total k-cut faces are finite. Independently computed alpha(S) for all 65536 subsets by vertex include/exclude dynamic programming; separately enumerated every independent k-set, all complementary facets and every nonempty subface, obtaining EXACT matching face sets. Rebuilt vertex-by-vertex acyclic matchings and topologically sorted EVERY Hasse edge: at k=4,5,6,7,8 respectively nonempty face counts 58670,39958,17574,4526,510; matched pairs 29070,19510,8566,2238,254; oriented cover counts 447600,274624,103792,22368,2032. Critical cells are one 0-cell plus 529 8-cells, 937 6-cells, 441 4-cells, 49 2-cells, and finally two 0-cells. The full acyclicity gives precisely the asserted integral wedges/sphere S0 by discrete Morse, not mere homology. Inspected certificate_q4_totalcut.json enumerates all critical masks and digests for match pairs; independent checked numbers match. No infinite extrapolation is made.

originality.rationale: Bayer et al. introduce total k-cut complexes, matching theorem and some graph families; the 4-cube is neither rectangular planar grid P4 x P4 nor K_{m,n}. Published Q4 total-3-cut result fully covers k=3 ONLY and explicitly not k>=4. Carnero Bravo 2026 §5.4 Question 53 asks higher total k-cut types of Cartesian products K_{n_i}; its theorem covers 2-cut products and does not include Q4 at k>=4. Five successive k levels complete a mathematically natural higher-end of this fixed graph tower, not mechanical recomputation of a known k>=4 table.
residual_risks: Unindexed high-k cube cut tables or unpublished precomputations could contain these exact five homotopy types, though the named recent product paper explicitly poses the broader question.
